newsitem.title: USA: USDA, FDA food transportation proposals near.
newsitem.headline: USDA, FDA food transportation proposals near.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department and the Food and Drug Administration are close to publishing preliminary proposals to regulate transportation of perishable food, a USDA official said Thursday.

Thomas Billy, associate administrator of USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service, said USDA and FDA aim to set temperature levels and other standards for storage and transportation of fresh meat, poultry, and other perishable foods.

The two agencies had finished making changes to the proposals requested by the White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB), and were about to resubmit them to OMB for final approval, Billy said.
The proposals take the form of an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, the first step in the regulatory process, which requests public comment on the initiative.
Billy was speaking after addressing a conference of the U.S. National Broiler Council outside Washington.
